assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of extreme coherence and accuracy, redefined precision measurement by pushing fractional uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a future redefinition of the second. A clear, concrete, high-impact instrument-and-concept achievement.
assessment.attribution: Two credited names fit a clean prize: Katori for the magic-wavelength lattice idea and first Sr lattice clock, Ye for the leading accuracy and stability demonstrations. Unresolved whether the single-ion clock lineage and frequency-comb metrology (already recognised in 2005 and 2012) need to be acknowledged in the citation.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many national metrology institutes; comparisons across continents are routine and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether credit should be shared with other lattice-clock groups or the ion-clock community is a judgement call from my background knowledge, not verified here.
Official redefinition of the SI second has not occurred, so practical impact is still maturing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Active-matter hydrodynamics established that collections of self-propelled units form a new class of nonequilibrium phases, with long-range order in two dimensions, giant number fluctuations and universal scaling. Vicsek's minimal model and the Toner-Tu theory are conceptually original and bring statistical-physics tools (renormalisation group, hydrodynamics) to a new domain. This is close to my own field, so I weigh it with care to avoid bias.
assessment.attribution: Vicsek (numerical flocking model), Toner (with Tu, the hydrodynamic theory and RG result) and Ramaswamy (active hydrodynamics of orientable fluids) are the three central figures. Yuhai Tu is not on the credited list, which leaves Toner's contribution somewhat incomplete; the three credited names still form a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of theory, simulation and experiments on bacteria, colloids and vibrated granular matter; the core predictions (giant number fluctuations) are confirmed, though precise scaling exponents remain debated.
uncertainties: Experimental verification of the exact 2D Toner-Tu exponents is incomplete.
Omission of Yuhai Tu from the credited names may distort fair attribution.
Breadth of the field makes the specific discovery cited somewhat diffuse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the HgTe observation, created the field of topological band insulators and shaped modern quantum materials research. Original, clear, and enormously influential for condensed matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical proposals (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall); Molenkamp led the experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells, building on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction, which is not in the credited list. Kane, Mele and Molenkamp form a defensible three-person set, though Zhang's contribution and the 3D materials work (Hasan, Moore, Balents, Fu) complicate fairness.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently in many materials and by transport and ARPES; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit split between 2D and 3D topological insulators and the role of Zhang and others remains unresolved.
Whether to prefer the B004 formulation with Xue's quantum anomalous Hall work is a separate question I do not rank.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Fluctuation theorems and the Jarzynski equality extend thermodynamics to small, driven systems, relating work fluctuations to equilibrium free energies and quantifying the arrow of time. Conceptually deep, widely used in single-molecule experiments and stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Evans, Cohen and Morriss (fluctuation theorem), Gallavotti and Cohen (chaotic hypothesis) and Jarzynski (equality) are central; Crooks and Kurchan are also important and are absent from the credited list, so a three-person configuration necessarily leaves out key contributors, with Jarzynski and Evans the most clearly decisive.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally verified in RNA/DNA pulling, colloids and recently quantum systems; stable and mature, though recognition may be considered more about theory than a discrete discovery.
uncertainties: Attribution is genuinely contested, and Crooks, Cohen and Kurchan are not credited.
Some may regard the result as an exact theoretical consequence rather than a physical discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory became the standard framework for strongly correlated electrons, giving a controlled treatment of the Mott transition and, combined with ab initio methods, of real materials. Originality is high (infinite-dimension limit, local self-energy) and impact lasting.
assessment.attribution: Metzner and Vollhardt introduced the large-dimension limit; Georges and Kotliar mapped it onto the Anderson impurity model; Müller-Hartmann also contributed. The credited trio is reasonable but excludes Metzner and Rozenberg, so allocation is partly unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Decades of use in oxides, heavy fermions and cold atoms; strong and independent validation, though a method rather than a single observation, and quantitative accuracy for finite-dimensional systems varies.
uncertainties: Method-based prizes are harder to cite as a discovery.
Credit for Metzner, Müller-Hartmann and Rozenberg is not accommodated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened moiré engineering of correlated and superconducting states, a new platform for flat-band physics. The theory predicted flat bands at the magic angle and experiments found correlated insulators and superconductivity; the impact has been rapid and broad.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group demonstrated the correlated and superconducting phases. Cory Dean, Yuan Cao and Kim's group also have strong claims, and Kim's and Dean's work on related states is outside the credited list, leaving the allocation open.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by multiple groups, though the nature of the superconductivity and many correlated states is still debated; recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and sample dependence remain unresolved.
Experimental credit is divided among several groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum error correction shows that fragile quantum information can be protected, underpinning fault-tolerant quantum computation. Shor's nine-qubit code and Steane's CSS code, together with Kitaev's topological codes, are foundational and conceptually elegant.
assessment.attribution: Shor and Steane independently discovered the first codes; Kitaev introduced fault tolerance via anyons. Calderbank, Gottesman, Knill, Laflamme and others also had decisive roles, so a three-person selection is somewhat arbitrary.
assessment.maturity: Recent experiments demonstrate below-threshold error correction in superconducting and atomic platforms, but practical fault tolerance has not been achieved. Recognition is arguably still somewhat premature, though the theory is mature.
uncertainties: Whether this is a physics discovery or computer science and information theory is arguable.
Large number of contributors makes the allocation contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The ATLAS and CMS discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and verified electroweak symmetry breaking, a landmark of experimental physics requiring decades of detector and accelerator development. Importance is beyond doubt.
assessment.attribution: The theory side was recognised in 2013; the experimental credit is spread over thousands of collaboration members. Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee are founding spokespersons and architects of the detectors, but this recognises leadership rather than a unique discovery, and individual attribution is delicate.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by two independent experiments and extensive measurements of couplings; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Fair allocation within very large collaborations is unresolved.
Recognition of the detector-design leaders rather than analysis leaders is debatable.
